articles.title: Christie Brinkley turned a 20-acre Hamptons estate into a private 'castle' with a greenhouse, pond and rewilded grounds
articles.summary: Christie Brinkley has spent more than two decades transforming her Bridgehampton estate into a private retreat that combines historic architecture with
articles.body: Christie Brinkley has spent more than two decades transforming her Bridgehampton estate into a private retreat that combines historic architecture with gardens, open grounds and unique features. Known as Tower Hill Estate, the property covers more than 20 acres and includes bedrooms, bathrooms across its main house and other buildings. Realtor reported that Brinkley gave real estate influencer Caleb Simpson a rare tour of the property, showing the spaces and outdoor areas that have made the estate one of the Hamptons’ distinctive homes.Christie Brinkley’s 20-acre Hamptons estate looks like a castleThe property’s castle-like appearance comes largely from its distinctive turret, which rises from the centre of the main residence. During the tour covered by Realtor, Simpson pointed out how the tower gives the house its castle appearance, while Brinkley herself described it more modestly as a little storybook house.Tower Hill Estate dates back to 1891, when it was built by local resident Dr John Gardiner. Brinkley bought the property in 1998, more than a century after it was constructed. Realtor noted that the house has since been restored with meticulous care, preserving its historic character while allowing it to function as a family home.The estate is spread across three parcels and contains considerably more than the main residence. The compound includes a 4-bedroom, 5-bathroom main house, a 4-bedroom guesthouse with two and a half bathrooms, a barn and art studio with living quarters, a four-car heated garage and a 50-foot observation deck.What makes the grounds different from a typical Hamptons estateBrinkley has given the land as much attention as the buildings. Realtor reported that she raises chickens on the property and is in the process of rewilding the grounds so that more flowers can grow across the estate.That approach is visible around the house, where the lawns and gardens form a major part of the setting. The original property listing described the grounds as park-like, with old specimen trees, winding walking paths and hills used for winter sledding. A private pond also forms part of the landscape, adding another natural feature to the expansive property.The estate also has a greenhouse with its own fireplace. During the tour, Brinkley showed the greenhouse and areas around the pool, where flower-filled planters add colour to the surroundings. She explained that the yard becomes filled with flowers in spring as the rewilding work continues.Why the estate feels like more than a historic houseThe property combines its old-world appearance with spaces designed for everyday family life. Inside, Realtor described soaring ceilings, large windows and plenty of natural light. The home includes an oversized country kitchen, a double-height great room, living and family rooms, three fireplaces, a gym and an office.A wisteria-covered pergola and multilevel stone terraces extend the living areas outdoors. There is also a heated pool with a spa, while the hidden tennis court gives the large estate another private recreational space.The interiors are not presented as a formal museum-like setting. Instead, Brinkley has filled the house with personal possessions and playful decorative touches. The dining room, for example, has a large round table, built-in storage, a bay window, chandeliers and paper lanterns, along with a neon dining room sign.How has Brinkley made the house feel personalThe tour also revealed several objects that reflect Brinkley’s personal connection with the property. Realtor reported that she showed a Broadway playbill that she considers her favourite cover she has ever done. She also pointed out a 270-year-old bonsai tree, joking about its age during the tour.The home has also been used for family gatherings. Brinkley showed the area where the family eats Thanksgiving dinner, giving the enormous property a more lived-in character despite its scale.The main residence is not the only place where the estate’s personality appears. The chickens that Brinkley keeps on the grounds have individual names, including Scrambled, Sunnyside Up and Benedict, adding an unexpectedly domestic touch to the sprawling property.What happened when Brinkley put the estate on the marketBrinkley has not always planned to remain at Tower Hill Estate. After owning the Bridgehampton property for about 20 years, she listed it in 2016 for $29.5 million. Realtor reported that she also put her Sag Harbor home on the market at the same time.The listings were part of an experiment. Brinkley planned to continue living in whichever of the two properties did not sell. Her Sag Harbor residence eventually found a buyer in February 2019, selling for just under its discounted $17.5 million asking price.That left Tower Hill Estate as her remaining Hamptons home. By the time of the Realtor report, Brinkley had lived there for 24 years and described it as the longest she had lived anywhere in her life.The observation tower provides perhaps the clearest reason the property has acquired its castle-like reputation. Rising above the main house, the turret offers wide views of the surrounding area and provides a final stop on Brinkley’s tour. The original listing also highlighted views extending towards the Atlantic Ocean and Connecticut Shore.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: 'Maintain peace for 1 year': CJP leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka released from detention
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: An executive magistrate court on Sunday released Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka from
articles.body: NEW DELHI: An executive magistrate court on Sunday released Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka from detention, a day after Delhi Police detained them following their arrival in the national capital ahead of a planned protest at Jantar Mantar.They were released on condition that they would not "breach peace" for a year, CJP legal affairs head Ratna Singh said.Advocate Soutik Banerjee also confirmed their release, saying, “All three (Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka, and Saurav Das) have been released. They can go from here.”Delhi Police said the three leaders were preventively arrested under Sections 126 and 170 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) on October 10. They were produced before the Sub-Divisional Executive Magistrate (SEM) court in Delhi Cantonment on Sunday, police said.“All due legal procedures were followed,” Delhi Police said, adding that a surety bond of Rs 50,000 was furnished to ensure peace and good behaviour for one year, following which the court released them.In a post on X after their release, CJP said, “Finally Delhi Police is forced to release Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das.”“Cockroaches never die,” the party added.The three leaders were detained by Delhi Police immediately after their flight landed in the national capital on Saturday and were subsequently placed under preventive arrest ahead of the planned protest at Jantar Mantar, police said.The detentions came amid a major security clampdown in Delhi. More than 7,000 protesters were detained at multiple locations, preventing them from reaching Jantar Mantar, police sources said.Several opposition leaders, including former chief ministers Arvind Kejriwal, Mamata Banerjee, Pinarayi Vijayan and Manik Sarkar, were also detained while attempting to join the protest.The CJP renewed its call for a protest at Jantar Mantar on Sunday as police continued security arrangements across the city. More than 30,000 police and paramilitary personnel were to be deployed, according to the report.The CJP and opposition parties have been demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter rolls.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Debt, abuse and restricted movement: 14 rescued from farms in suspected bonded labour cases in Rajasthan
articles.summary: 14 people, including eight minors, were rescued from farms in Nagaur, Bikaner and Ajmer in suspected bonded labour cases, alleging debt traps, abuse and restricted movement.
articles.body: Jaipur: Fourteen people, including eight minors, were rescued in three suspected bonded labour cases in Nagaur, Bikaner and Ajmer within one week in Sept this year. Families alleged that they were trapped in debt and not allowed to leave farms. They also reported verbal abuse, physical assault and children being forced to work.The families had migrated from their hometowns in search of work. They were rescued following complaints filed by their relatives.This year India marks 50 years of the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976, with govt aiming to identify and release all bonded labourers by 2030.In Nagaur, six family members, including four children, were rescued from a farm in Chappri village, Merta, on Sept 26. They belonged to Jayal in Nagaur and Bhopalgarh in Jodhpur.Ramniwas Nayak said his family had taken an advance of Rs 1.5 lakh, but outstanding debt allegedly rose to Rs 2.45 lakh over 1.5 years despite five family members working on the farm.“Pabandi puri thi, kahi aane jaane nahi deta,” he said, alleging that the owner restricted their movement, threatened them with a gun and prevented them from attending even family funerals. He also alleged that the owner assaulted him on Sept 24. This led to a complaint by Ramniwas’s brother on Sept 25.SDM Sunil Kumar said an investigation was underway and further action would follow if a bonded labour case was established.In Bikaner, six members of a family from Anupgarh, Sri Ganganagar, were rescued from a farm in Akhoosar on Sept 29. The family included three minors.Hariram said his family worked on a farm for nearly five years, but he could never repay the debt as the employer kept adding other expenses to the loan. “My employer would sell crops I grew and never gave me an account of the proceeds. Five of us worked on the farm, yet he would still say that our earnings are deducted from loan,” Hari Ram said.He alleged that his children were also made to work and that the family was denied freedom to leave.“I was kept in severe bondage and suffered immensely,” he said. “Mere bacche anpadh hi reh gaye” (My children remained illiterate), he added, alleging that restrictions on movement prevented them from obtaining identity documents for children and enrolling them in school. The complaint about the family’s situation was filed by Hariram’s brother-in-law on Sept 28.However, Bikaner SDM Sanwarmal Regar said, “The complaint appeared to be motivated. Sharecropping is practiced in this area, and our investigation found no evidence of bonded labour. The person who filed the complaint does not reside in the area. We rescued the family and directed the farm owner to send them home. The family had come to work under a sharecropping arrangement, and no case of bonded labour was established in our inquiry.”In Ajmer, a father and his 15-year-old son were rescued on Oct 1. Shivraj Bheel had allegedly borrowed Rs 45,000 for medical expenses in 2023, after which his son was sent to work as a cow keeper. Shivraj later joined him when the debt amount allegedly rose to Rs 75,000 with interests. He said the owner refused to let him return home when his father suffered a heart attack in Sept 2026, prompting him to file a complaint against the owner on Sept 30.
